page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz. It features 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading to supply 4 dedicated virtual CPUs. The memory allocation stands at 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The cache structure consists of 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Advanced hardware extensions are present, including AVX-512 (f, vnni, and bf16 variants), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance operates under a KVM hypervisor, includes no local storage, and provides a baseline network speed of 4 Gbps without discrete GPU hardware.

Performance benchmark results show strong single-threaded CPU efficiency. Stress-ng single-core performance reaches 3112.38, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances, while the Geekbench single-core score of 2017.0 and text processing score of 2537.0 fall into the top 25%. Multi-core metrics align with middle-tier expectations, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 6228.1, Geekbench multi-core reaching 4558.0, and PassMark CPU scoring 7636.06. Memory bandwidth for large block uncached operations registers at 47.72 GB/sec for reads and 28.11 GB/sec for writes.

The hardware configuration exhibits tradeoffs in memory-intensive and concurrent data tasks. Small-block cached memory bandwidth (307.69 GB/sec), software compilation via Clang (5568.0), and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (26.74 GB/sec) test in the bottom 25%. Application-level benchmarks indicate lower throughput for data-centric roles, with Redis SET operations at 5.71 million operations per second, PassMark database operations at 2093.43, and static web serving throughput at 5.46 GB/sec. The instance is suited for general application hosting, light microservices, and single-threaded processing scripts where high memory throughput and local disk performance are not primary requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.xlarge is a general-purpose instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs from a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor, 16.0 GB of memory, and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no local storage or attached GPUs. The instance demonstrates strong single-core compute performance, highlighted by top-tier stress-ng and top 25% Geekbench single-core benchmark scores. Conversely, multi-core metrics sit at system averages, while small-block memory bandwidth, Redis key-value operations, static web serving throughput, and database transaction benchmarks fall into the lower quartile. This profile makes the instance effective for single-threaded processing jobs, microservices, and general application hosting that do not demand high memory throughput or heavy local disk operations.
